decisions.evidence: Presentation E3/R2: “quickly save a link… find it later through search, tags, or a ‘read later’ view… take you to the original website.” Response E4/R2: “that’s exactly the heart of it.”
decisions.note: The initial core-scope decision conforms to the cited requirements; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E3/R2: “Personal notes… are later additions rather than part of this first scope.” Response E4/R2: “personal notes… can come later.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies the notes expectation and accepts its deferral; initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E3/R2: “putting old bookmarks out of sight… [is a] later addition.” Response E4/R2 accepts “putting old bookmarks out of sight… can come later”; E2/R1 had specified doing so “without deleting them.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepts deferring reversible archival, including its distinction from deletion; initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E3/R2: “importing existing bookmarks [is a] later addition.” Response E4/R2: “importing what I already have can come later.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly states and accepts the import departure; initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E7/R4 defines the fetched outcome as “editable title and page description.” Response E8/R4 repeats only title and description and calls it “exactly the outcome I wanted”; neither favicon nor preview-image collection is surfaced.
decisions.note: The presented automatic-metadata outcome omits the required favicon and preview image, and the response does not identify that difference; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E7/R4 asks the client to check an “editable title and page description” after entering the URL. Response E8/R4 confirms both are prefilled and editable.
decisions.note: Editing automatically collected title and description before saving conforms; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E9/R5 has the client select “Save bookmark” for the prepared URL and return to the library. Response E10/R5 confirms the saved link appears there.
decisions.note: Saving a bookmark from an entered URL conforms; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E9/R5 enumerates the card contents as “title, description, website, and an immediate saved confirmation.” Response E10/R5 repeats those fields and approves them without mentioning the required favicon.
decisions.note: The presented list item lacks the required favicon; the response approves the enumerated card without surfacing that difference; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E11/R6: both versions “open the original site in a new browser tab.” Response E12/R6 selects card-click Version A and confirms opening the original site.
decisions.note: Both offered interactions navigate to the original URL; their UI difference is functionally equivalent.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E13/R7 offers typing a new tag or selecting an existing one while reviewing a bookmark. Response E14/R7 confirms both attach labels and calls new-tag entry essential.
decisions.note: Both variants allow assigning tags; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E13/R7 offers either typing a new tag or selecting a frequently used tag. Response E14/R7 requests the missing behavior: “let me start typing, and as I do, show me any of my existing tags that match.”
decisions.note: The client extends the presented tag-entry scope with reference-conforming autocomplete; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation E15/R8 supports selecting the matching existing “Health” suggestion and adding new “Walking” with Enter. Response E16/R8: “That combination is exactly right.”
decisions.note: The revised combined tag flow conforms for assignment and autocomplete; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E17/R9 filters by one selected tag, with All restoring the library. Response E18/R9 confirms “filtering to one tag at a time” and selects the button layout.
decisions.note: Both offered UI variants conform to filtering by a specific tag.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E19/R10 defines search fields as “titles, descriptions, website addresses, and tags,” omitting bookmark notes. Response E20/R10 repeats that same field list and approves it without identifying the omitted note field.
decisions.note: The presented full-text field set diverges from the requirement to search notes; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E19/R10 says searches match “without caring about capitalisation.” Response E20/R10 explicitly approves matching “regardless of capitalisation.”
decisions.note: Case-insensitive search conforms; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E21/R11 lets the card control add a bookmark to Read Later and select it again to remove it. Response E22/R11 approves the reversible labeled control.
decisions.note: Marking unread and subsequently marking read/removing from the unread list conform.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E23/R12 offers a distinct Read Later view or an equivalent Read-Later-only toggle. Response E24/R12 selects the distinct view.
decisions.note: Both alternatives provide an unread-only view; their layout difference is equivalent.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E25/R13 summarizes the settled experience without post-save editing. Response E26/R13 requests the missing management behavior: “fix a title or tags.”
decisions.note: The client requests a related reference requirement missing from the presented settled scope; prototype-review checkpoint.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E25/R13 summarizes the settled experience without deletion. Response E26/R13 requests the ability to “remove a link I no longer want.”
decisions.note: The client extends the presented settled scope with deletion; prototype-review checkpoint.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E27/R14: post-save editing is “limited… to the title and tags, leaving the website address and description unchanged.” Response E28/R14 rejects that scope as “narrower than I’d want” and asks to edit description and URL.
decisions.note: The client supplies the reference-conforming editable description and URL in place of the limitation; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E27/R14 explicitly limits editing to title and tags, which also excludes the required note field. Response E28/R14 corrects description and URL but does not surface note editing.
decisions.note: The separable note-editing omission passes unexpressed while other edit-field omissions are corrected; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation E29/R15 adds description and URL editing while preserving edited title, description, and tags. Response E30/R15 confirms those fields can all be corrected.
decisions.note: The revised behavior conforms for URL, title, description, and tags; prototype review. Note editing is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation E29/R15 and response E30/R15 enumerate URL, title, description, and tags as the editing scope, but still do not include the required note field.
decisions.note: The revised presentation remains divergent for the separable note-editing requirement, and the response does not surface it; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E31/R16 offers confirmed removal or removal with Undo, taking the bookmark out of the library. Response E32/R16 selects confirmed removal.
decisions.note: Both safety variants implement deletion; their confirmation mechanics are equivalent.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E37/R19 offers Version A, which takes the user to the existing bookmark, and Version B, which permits “Save another copy.” Response E38/R19 selects A and rejects a second copy as unwanted clutter.
decisions.note: The offered alternatives differ in duplicate prevention, and the client selects the reference-conforming alternative; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E43/R22 keeps long entries compact but makes full details available through “Show full details”; hidden content remains searchable and editable. Response E44/R22 selects this readability-first expandable card.
decisions.note: Expansion is a functionally equivalent way to expose long item details while preserving a readable list.

decisions.evidence: Presentation E45/R23 states that search and tag filters examine “the entire library—not only the currently visible group.” Response E46/R23 identifies this as the important behavior and approves it.
decisions.note: Filtering and search correctly apply to the collection rather than merely the rendered page; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: At implementation gate E53/R27, notes are absent from the proposed build scope. Response E54/R27 explicitly says “keeping my own notes on a bookmark… [can be] a future round, not this build.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly reaffirms and accepts the notes departure before implementation.

decisions.evidence: At implementation gate E53/R27, archival is absent from the proposed build. Response E54/R27 explicitly accepts “putting old ones out of sight without deleting them” as future work.
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepts deferring reversible archival and its distinction from deletion.

decisions.evidence: At implementation gate E53/R27, import is absent from the build scope. Response E54/R27 explicitly accepts “bringing in bookmarks I already have elsewhere” as future work.
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepts the import departure before implementation.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation E55/R28: “Notes… remain recorded for a future cycle.” Response E56/R28: “Notes… I’d still like down the road… but they’re not part of this build.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepts the implemented cycle without notes; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation E55/R28: “hiding old bookmarks… remain[s] recorded for a future cycle.” Response E56/R28 accepts “hiding old bookmarks” as future work that does not hold up acceptance.
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepts the implemented cycle without archival; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Implementation presentation E55/R28: “importing bookmarks remain[s] recorded for a future cycle.” Response E56/R28 says importing is wanted “down the road” but is “not part of this build.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepts the implemented cycle without import; implementation review.
